description:
The measurement dataset behind the accompanying software record: every aggregated result the paper's claims are recomputed from.

Contents: the campaign ledger (one row per instrumented-benchmark cell: configuration, sign-separated discard counters, log size and SHA-256 of the source log); per-cell counter extracts; the Python-harness results (per-cell counts with sign-separated discards and per-run pacer-jitter percentiles, same-host and cross-host); the grid-membership inference output; the minute-by-minute clock-discipline log; the distributed-mode failure diagnostics; and the per-experiment CSVs for the negative-span campaigns (audit, priority, geometry, payload, trace).

Headline totals: 223 instrumented OpenMessaging Benchmark runs; Kafka-driver corpus 10,913,263 discarded samples with 0 negatives; Redis-driver corpus 619,229 with 41,403 negatives, every one exactly -1000 microseconds. The schema is documented in the software record's supplement (S3).

New in v2.5. Three artefact families were added across the Transactions on Computers revision rounds, each generated by a committed script and pinned by tests. (1) span_recount.csv: the per-run, per-span negative counts and extrema behind the headroom exclusion — 5,913 runs and 738,730 producer-consumer events, the acknowledgement-referenced span going negative in 4,549 runs while the send-referenced span never does, with per-run minima that bound any same-host clock offset at +220 µs. (2) external/harness_registry.csv: the audited-harness evidence, one verified source line per finding with file, symbol, URL and read date, whose class labels are recomputed on every build rather than stored. (3) external/grid_membership.csv: the per-arm permutation inference behind the grid-membership figure and table. The platform probe additionally records clocksource provenance (current_clocksource, the available list, and TSC flags) for any future run, a field the reported campaigns lacked and the manuscript discloses as bounded rather than recorded.

New in v2. Three artefact families were added for the IEEE TPDS revision, each generated by a committed script and pinned by tests. (1) traced_tail_slope.csv: survival, local slopes and windowed log-log indices recovered from the traced bpftrace run-queue histogram, giving a second and independent estimator of the stall tail (0.332 over 0.25-2 ms) against the 0.339 fitted from the payload sweep. (2) Audit-gated powered-transport artefacts (*_gated.csv in transport_rt/ and transport_rt2/) plus gate_sensitivity.csv: the earlier powered comparison had consumed audit-condemned runs, so the primary tables are now computed on audit-surviving runs only, with the sensitivity of the conclusion to that choice reported rather than asserted. (3) first_result_threshold_sweep.csv: a condition-level sweep showing that no cell of the withdrawn first result set becomes fully usable at any audit threshold up to 20%.

A SHA256SUMS manifest lists every file in the archive so any single file can be verified independently of the zip.

Data note. No StatsBomb event data is included. Aggregate workload statistics derived from it remain subject to StatsBomb's CC BY-NC 4.0 terms with attribution.

Licence. This data compilation and its documentation are released under CC BY 4.0. The analysis code that produced and consumes it is MIT and lives in the linked software record; the manuscript files archived there are the authors' copyright and are expressly not CC BY, pending journal publication.

v2.6. The measurements are unchanged from v2.5 — no campaign was re-run and no value moved. This version is re-cut from the v2.6.0 tag so that the dataset and the software record, which now derives every printed quantity from these files, are the same commit.

v2.7. No campaign was re-run and no measurement re-taken; what is new here is derived. Five artefact families are added, each generated by a committed script and pinned by tests. (1) The per-event span decomposition — span_symmetry.csv, span_run_level.csv, span_histogram.csv and their JSON summaries — which carries S = D − A per event, the producer-side displacement A, and the recovery estimator's error split by whether the run passed or failed the sign check, because a correction validated only where the check already passes has been validated on the population that did not need it. (2) ρ(D, A) in span_symmetry.csv, now a windowed Pearson correlation on paired co-moments; the previous variance-identity estimator neither conserved nor stayed bounded, returning |ρ| > 1 on five of seventy conditions. (3) stall_mixture.json, the two-state fit behind the scheduling account. (4) omb_published_quantiles.csv, the published figures the grid law is checked against. (5) uncertainty_audit.csv. external/harness_registry.csv is extended to the harnesses practitioners actually run — SPECjms2007, the Kafka bundled tools, RabbitMQ PerfTest, nats bench and Redpanda rpk — each with a verified source line for what it does about timestamp resolution and sign. Re-cut from the v2.7.0 tag so that the dataset and the software record remain the same commit.

What changed in v3.0. The record's creator list goes from two names to four: R. Duvignau and N. Herbst join as authors of the accompanying work. No measurement, estimate or interval in this dataset differs from v2.7.0; the contents are re-cut from the v3.0.0 tag so that the dataset and the software record remain the same commit.
